description: Exact selected original GenuTax interview definitions; no real taxpayer data. Original prompts are preserved as reverse engineering evidence, not interpreted as answers.

maritalChanges.covers: previous tax year, current tax year and following tax year
maritalChanges.caution: A year-end status alone does not capture changes affecting benefit eligibility and spousal calculations. No is an explicit factual answer, never a universal default.

spouse.manualNetIncomeDefinition: Line 23600 of spouse return, or what it would be if filed; separation/part-year rules in original prompt apply. Not gross income or total income.
spouse.derivedNote: Computed by engine; do not supply as an input. Native2021 coupled probe matches spouse computed T1GEN:00236:C.
spouse.totalIncome: No general manual spouse-total-income input in selected spouse interview section. For a coupled return, spouse total income is calculated from spouseFields and available as spouseFields T1GEN:00150:C.

coupledReturns.requirements: Complete year-specific spouse input map, including own TAXPY DOB, residency and MARST. Both returns must be appropriate to prepare together; original interview excludes different year-end province/territory/country.
coupledReturns.observed: Native calculator receives primary/spouse Hashtable arguments; PerformCalc calculates both and mirrors spouse DOB/net income. Manual spouseFields=null leaves manual SPOUS fields as inputs.
coupledReturns.warning: Do not treat an empty/partial spouseFields object as a known-zero-income spouse. Household linking, completeness and consent are separate application concerns.

topics.title: Preparing Returns Together
paragraphs: You are able to prepare your tax return and your spouse's or common-law partner's tax return at the same time. Doing so will allow GenuTax Standard to optimize your tax returns so that you are both claiming the maximum amount of deductions and credits to which you are entitled.

Of course, this is not always possible. For instance, you may have separated due to a breakdown in your relationship since the end of [METAD:00001:I], and, therefore, may not have access to your spouse's or common-law partner's tax information.

Also note that you cannot prepare your returns at the same time if you and your spouse or common-law partner were not resident in the same province or territory (or country) as of December 31, [METAD:00001:I].
Click the button below to prepare your spouse's or common-law partner's return at the same time as preparing your own return.

topics.title: Spouse's or Common-law Partner's Net Income
paragraphs: Enter your spouse's or common-law partner's net income for [METAD:00001:I].

This is the amount on line 23600 of your spouse's or common-law partner's tax return, or the amount that it would be if he or she filed a tax return. This amount is used when calculating certain tax credits and benefits that you may be entitled to.

Note: If you separated during [METAD:00001:I] because of a breakdown in your relationship, and were not back together on December 31, [METAD:00001:I], enter only your spouse's or common-law partner's net income for the period before the separation.
